unresolved.finding: MPI return codes from communicator, datatype, collective, point-to-point, and free operations are never checked.
A root-contract violation aborts MPI_COMM_WORLD rather than the communicator supplied by the caller.
Vector distribution creates subarray datatypes from unchecked is/lm metadata and destination extent, permitting invalid starts or subsizes.
Block-vector distribution independently uses size(a,2) for send types and size(b,2) for receive types without verifying equality, so sender and receiver type signatures can disagree.
All matrix distribution and collection implementations depend on genmpi_distr.inc and genmpi_coll.inc, but neither include exists under source_code.
decomp divides and takes modulo by numprocs without rejecting zero and does not validate myid.
det_submatrices assumes output arrays have at least mp*np elements and dimensions exceed the fixed four-cell overlap without validating either condition.
Border shifting indexes second and penultimate rows/columns and uses ma-2 counts without checking minimum matrix dimensions.
MPI status codes are consistently captured but not checked, so communication failures can leave partially populated arrays or enter later waits with invalid requests.
Vector distribution indexes is/lm by communicator size and copies lm elements into b without validating metadata extents, source ranges, or destination capacity.
Scatter variants trust is/lm/js/ln and local matrix shapes completely, allowing invalid displacements, counts, or b columns to be passed to MPI.
Both column-send root loops terminate only after incrementing sends, so a valid zero-total workload makes the unbounded loop advance j forever.
The send variants allocate a full bb copy on the root even though bb is only read on non-root processes.
Whole-matrix distribution computes array sections from unchecked metadata and root rank before validating that source and destination shapes match.
Shape mismatches abort MPI_COMM_WORLD rather than the communicator passed to the routine, unexpectedly terminating unrelated ranks in an embedded or split-communicator use.

Column collection derives counts, receive totals, and array sections from unchecked overlap flags and metadata, so inconsistent flags can produce negative counts, missing receives, or out-of-bounds sections.
Whole-submatrix collectors subtract a fixed four-cell overlap without enforcing local dimensions of at least four, allowing negative extents and MPI counts.
decomp divides and takes modulo by numprocs without rejecting zero, and does not validate myid against the process range.
det_submatrices assumes all eight output arrays contain at least mp*np elements and that ma/na exceed the fixed overlap, but validates neither condition.
Border shifting forms rows/columns 2 and ma-1/na-1 and uses count ma-2 without checking that the matrix has sufficient dimensions.
getparametertype_c always returns success zero and does not validate the index returned by getkey_indextype, so an unknown parameter can return an undefined type code as a successful query.
Several Fortran wrappers assign the fixed 1024-element result of string_to_char_array into automatic arrays sized only len(name) or len(name)+1, which is a nonconforming whole-array assignment.
Parameter and array name lookup index allocatable key/state tables directly without checking the caller-supplied index range.

C entry points pass variable-length name arrays to char_array_to_string, whose dummy contract reads up to 1024 elements, so length-sized buffers without an in-range NUL can be read beyond their declared extent.
Numeric parameter getters do not verify myparam's type before reading r0 or i0, so calling a getter with a valid name of the wrong type accesses the wrong parameter component.
getcharparameter returns early on lookup failure without setting valuelength or initializing the output buffer.
Array type and rank queries return on an unknown name without initializing their output arguments.
getarraydimsize_c initializes its status to -1 and never sets it to zero after successfully computing dimsize, so every call reports failure.
Dimension-size lookup rejects only dim values greater than rank; zero or negative dimensions pass through and can reach SIZE with an invalid DIM argument, while rank-1 lookup ignores dim entirely.
Generic and rank-specific array entry points validate only the mnemonic, not that the selected array's type and rank match the routine, before dereferencing a specific pointer component.
Scalar C getters return c_loc of an unsaved local target, so the pointer becomes undefined as soon as the function returns.
Array C getters return pointers into one saved scratch allocation per rank and deallocate that allocation on the next same-rank getter call, but this short lifetime is not exposed in the API.
All C array setters convert and dereference the incoming c_ptr without checking c_associated or receiving a buffer length, so null or undersized caller buffers cannot be rejected.
Integer setters exist through rank 2 only and only ranks 0 and 1 are exposed through the module generic, while array metadata can report higher-rank integer arrays.
strlen returns zero both for an empty string and for a full 1024-byte array with no NUL terminator, so unterminated input is silently misinterpreted as empty.
strcmp constructs both string1 and string2 from char_array1, causing every comparison to report equality.
strcmp trims both converted strings and uses Fortran lexical comparison, which does not preserve ordinary C strcmp behavior for spaces preceding the NUL.
strcpy relies on the ambiguous zero returned by strlen, so an unterminated source copies only its first character and does not guarantee a terminator in the destination.
string_to_char_array does not cap len_trim to MAXSTRINGLEN-1, so strings of length 1024 or more write beyond the result when data and the terminator are stored.
string_to_char_array initializes only the payload and one terminator, leaving the remainder of its fixed 1024-element result undefined.
Module state is saved globally and init has no already-initialized guard or cleanup path, so repeated initialization can reinitialize MPI and reallocate persistent model/output state.
outputext assigns its function result only when module error is exactly 0 or 1, leaving the C-visible return value undefined for any other error code.
The optional custom timestep has neither intent nor value semantics, leaving its mutation and language-binding contract unclear to callers.
executestep sets error through timestep and skips physics on failure, but then unconditionally increments the completed-step count and returns success zero.
Output schedules and progress logging are advanced immediately after timestep reports an error, before the error guard that suppresses the physical update.
MPI finalization passes saved t01 to timing output even though t01 is assigned only when execute_counter equals 1, so short or failed runs can finalize with an undefined loop-start timestamp.
final has no initialized/finalized guard and always finalizes logging and MPI, making duplicate finalization or finalization before successful init unsafe.
getversion silently truncates to the caller's fixed length and provides no explicit NUL termination or returned required length despite using c_char storage.
C-int wrapper results are assigned directly from default-integer library functions without an explicit kind conversion or assertion that the kinds match.
This module exports the C symbol finalize with a different wrapper from xbeach_bmi.f90, so the build must keep the two objects mutually exclusive but that requirement is not expressed in the source.
The exported writetolog test calls distributelog unconditionally even though that procedure pointer is initialized null and may never have been assigned.
A C-exported function emits the same hard-coded test message ten times, exposing apparent test scaffolding as part of the library ABI.
The procedure interface used for a C function pointer is not declared bind(C), so c_f_procpointer does not establish a portable interoperable callback calling convention.
The module includes writeloginterface.inc and writelog.inc, but neither file exists under source_code, leaving the logging API dependent on absent generated artifacts.
start_logfiles never initializes error to zero, leaves it untouched on non-master ranks, and later tests it on every rank.
Log-file OPEN statements have no iostat checks, while the reported error is based only on whether a positive unit number was found, so actual open failures are not detected.
progress_indicator does not require positive dper, dt, or count_rate; in particular dper=0 reaches mod(curper,dper) and divides by zero.
The saved system_clock baseline does not account for count_max rollover, which can suppress time-based progress reports after wraparound.
The error-6 warning describes an excessive N-direction split but tells the user to reduce MPI domains in the M direction.
Final timing divides by timestep count n without guarding n=0, affecting both average timestep and performance calculations.
assignlogdelegate_internal declares local integer i but never uses it, suggesting incomplete delegate setup or stale code.
NetCDF error handling always attempts to close module variable ncid, even when the failing operation is file creation and ncid may not yet contain a valid handle.

The NetCDF-only initializer never initializes saved output counters, while ncoutput increments them and uses itd directly as the drifter record index; those counters are initialized only by fortoutput_init.
The dimension expression s%ntdisch is mapped to a hard-coded NetCDF dimension of length 2, despite the expression denoting runtime state and no equality check being made.
Global variable setup passes unchecked mnemonic indices to indextos, and an unsupported type leaves its ID at -1 but still proceeds to attach attributes to that invalid ID.
Point-variable setup reads dimensions(1) and dimensions(2) before verifying rank is at least 2, so a scalar or rank-1 selection accesses dimension metadata out of bounds.
A point variable whose first two dimensions are not x and y only produces a log message and is still defined and later sampled as a spatial field.
Point initialization creates IDs only for real variables, but the default branch merely prints for other types and then unconditionally uses the uninitialized pointsvarids entry for attributes.
Rank errors while defining mean variables report mnem even though that variable is not assigned in the mean-variable loop and can contain stale text from an earlier loop.
pointtypes is written to the same NetCDF variable twice consecutively.
Point/runup processing is conditioned on npointvar being positive, so a valid runup-only configuration with gauges but no ordinary point variables never writes point time or runup output.
Point extraction passes unchecked mnemonic indices to indextos and accepts an unchecked owner rank from space_who_has before point-to-point communication.
The non-MPI rank-4 point path allocates its third dimension from t%r3 instead of t%r4, potentially dereferencing an unassociated pointer and producing the wrong shape.
Global, point, and mean NetCDF times are always multiplied by morfac, whereas the rest of the module and BMI time API apply that scaling only when morfacopt equals 1.
Integer global variables are defined for ranks 0 through 4 during initialization, but writing omits ranks 1 and 4 and only prints a message, leaving their records unwritten.
Rank-1 real output allocates and deallocates r1 without ever using it, doubling temporary allocation work alongside r1conv.
NetCDF point output for rank-3 and rank-4 variables writes only element (1,1,1) or (1,1,1,1) while the variables were defined with full trailing dimensions, leaving all other components unwritten.

Fortran-compatible rank-3 and rank-4 point output reads local temporaries r3 and r4 on the I/O path even though extracted values were stored in pointoutputs and those temporaries have already been deallocated or were never allocated there.
The runup-file loop writes unit indexed by ii but flushes unit indexed by stale variable i, potentially flushing an unrelated or unconnected unit.
thetamean output applies a legacy packed-value decoding expression even though the active averaging code stores a direct atan2 angle, corrupting both NetCDF and Fortran angular means.
The next averaging interval is updated only inside the Fortran-compatible output branch, so NetCDF-only runs retain the configured nominal interval even when the final or scheduled interval differs.
Drifter NetCDF time is written as raw par%t while global, point, and mean time coordinates in the same file use morphological scaling, producing inconsistent time axes when scaling is active.
Fortran point files are opened directly from unchecked station IDs, with no rejection of duplicate, blank, truncated, or path-containing names that can collide or target unintended relative files.
Fortran mean-file record lengths are always derived from real pointer components even though the averaging initializer permits integer mean variables.
Lazily opened global Fortran files omit status='replace', so an existing longer file from a prior run can retain stale trailing records.
All hotstart writers capture OPEN iostat but never check it and then perform unguarded writes and close operations; they also omit replacement semantics for existing files.
Output-format selection has no default case, so an unexpected format value silently skips all format-specific initialization.
The hotstart message is emitted whenever outputh is set and hotstart writing is enabled, before this module has evidence that creation actually succeeded.
output_error claims an extra output timestep is created, but the output call is commented out and the routine immediately halts without using any of its state arguments.

Output-variable validation passes chartoindex results directly to indextos and has no default rejection for unknown types or ranks outside 0 through 4, allowing malformed selections to bypass the association checks.

Allocation errors are broadcast and halted only within the compute communicator, while the separate I/O rank retains outputError zero, so the I/O process is not explicitly brought into this failure path.
Progress and completion-time calculations divide by par%tstop without guarding a zero stop time.
log_progress keeps firsttime and timing accumulators in saved procedure state with no reset, so a second model run in the same process inherits the prior run's wall-clock baseline.

snappointstogrid sizes work storage from parameter counts but does not verify the extents of xpoints, ypoints, coordinate arrays, pointtypes, or optional dmin before indexed or whole-array assignment.
gridrotate_r2 allocates and zeroes two full-grid automatic transport arrays on every call even for variable names that never use them, creating avoidable stack and runtime pressure for large domains.

The rank-2, rank-3, and rank-4 rotation routines dereference optional col whenever positive row is present without checking col is present; rank 3 and 4 also leave all section indices uninitialized when row is present but nonpositive.
Row/column point-selection accepts unchecked indices and assumes a destination with at least a 1x1 leading section.
When rotation is disabled, the Sutot and Svtot cases compute a temporary transport field but never assign it to x, leaving the intent(out) result undefined.
gridrotate_r3 merely logs mismatched leading dimensions between alfaz and t%r3 and then continues into conforming-array assignments and indexed expressions that require those dimensions to match.
gridrotate_r3 creates and zeroes five full rank-3 automatic arrays for every call regardless of the selected variable, risking substantial stack use.
runup assigns result elements only where pointtypes equals 1, so all ordinary point elements are returned uninitialized.

The source itself marks runup incorrect, and its implementation assigns every gauge the same scalar derived from the first global minimum location of wetz rather than determining runup along each gauge line.
means_init passes chartoindex results directly to index allocation and lookup without rejecting an unknown mean-variable index.
Initialization handles only ranks 2 through 4 and has no default rejection, leaving unsupported requested ranks with unallocated accumulator pointers.
All local integer-array initialization branches obtain dimensions from the real pointer components r2/r3/r4 instead of i2/i3/i4, which may be unassociated and is not the selected variable storage.
The averaging weight evaluates par%dt/par%tintm before max can clamp it, so a zero averaging interval still causes division by zero.

The near-zero circular-mean guard computes numeps*sign(tvar2d_cos,1.d0), which remains zero when cosine is zero and is far below numeps otherwise, so it does not reliably prevent the invalid atan2(0,0) case.
The saved circular accumulators tvar2d_sin and tvar2d_cos are never reset by clearaverage, so later averaging periods include all prior periods even though the published mean arrays are cleared.

Rank-3 averaging always sizes temporaries from t%r3 and calls the real grid-rotation path even though means_init explicitly permits rank-3 integer variables, making integer selections dereference the wrong component.
Rank-4 temporary dimensions 1 through 3 are taken from t%r3 rather than t%r4, so a normal rank-4 variable can dereference an unassociated rank-3 pointer or allocate the wrong shape.
makecrossvector indexes every requested variable through r2/i2 at mg and assigns it into a caller section without validating variable rank, mg bounds, or destination extent.
initialize converts the caller-supplied configuration path into configfile but never uses it, so the BMI configuration argument has no effect on model initialization.
update overwrites the executestep return code with outputext's return code unconditionally, masking a failed timestep whenever outputext returns success.
get_var_type returns without setting c_type_name when chartoindex fails and also converts an uninitialized type_name for an unexpected type code.
get_var_rank returns without assigning the output rank when the requested variable name is unknown.
The module includes get_var_shape.inc, get_var.inc, and set_var.inc, but none is present anywhere under source_code, leaving the BMI variable API dependent on missing generated artifacts.
set_current_time converts and dereferences an arbitrary incoming c_ptr without checking c_associated, so a null pointer from the C caller is invalid.
Morphological time conversion silently substitutes 1 for any morfac below 1, making set/get time behavior diverge from the configured factor without reporting invalid configuration.
The nominal get_time_step query calls compute_dt on live model state before returning par%dt, so its read-only BMI contract is unclear and repeated queries may alter timestep-related state.
The module unconditionally initializes and finalizes MPI without checking existing MPI state, conflicting with embedding hosts that own the MPI lifecycle.

The I/O rank deliberately has xmpi_comm set to MPI_COMM_NULL, yet normal halt and communicator error handling call xmpi_abort on xmpi_comm, so an error on that rank can attempt MPI_Abort with an invalid communicator instead of terminating the full job.
Processor-grid scoring uses default-integer products and a fixed 1000000000 sentinel, allowing large domain dimensions to overflow or leave a valid factorization unselected.
Manual decomposition checks only the product, so two negative manual dimensions can pass and later become invalid divisors and neighbor geometry.
The XPREF condition can evaluate m/nmin when integer division n/xmpi_size produced zero, because Fortran does not require short-circuit evaluation of .and., yielding a division by zero.
Cyclic boundary handling has cases only for 0 and 1 and no default, so any other cyclic value leaves negative or out-of-range neighbor ranks marked as non-boundaries.

Fourteen broadcast wrappers include xmpi_bcast.inc, but that include is absent from the source_code tree, leaving these procedures uncompilable unless an undocumented external generation step supplies it.
Eight-byte integer broadcast uses nonstandard integer*8 syntax and the nonportable MPI_INTEGER8 datatype rather than a kind-matched MPI type.
Character broadcast does not verify that non-source character variables can hold the source's trimmed length before assigning x(i:i).
All sendrecv overloads reuse size(sendbuf) as the receive count without checking recvbuf size, permitting receive truncation or overwrite for mismatched arguments.
Array reductions send size(x) elements into y without asserting equal extents, leaving root receive-buffer capacity implicit.
Basic shift routines directly reference rows or columns 2, m-1, and n-1 without validating minimum local-array extents.
Ranged shift routines accept arbitrary i1/i2 and derive sections from a fixed four-cell overlap without checking ordering or bounds.

The paired send helpers derive counts independently from each rank's local array and do not validate from/to ranks, so shape disagreement or invalid endpoints can cause truncation or indefinite blocking.
xmpi_send_sleep ignores all MPI errors and polls forever until flag becomes true, so a failed Irecv or MPI_Test has no exit path.
xmpi_barrier defaults to xmpi_comm even though that communicator is MPI_COMM_NULL on the I/O process, and the procedure contains no guard against invocation there.
xmpi_getrow does not validate prow, n, size(a,2), or size(b), so inconsistent metadata can produce invalid ranks, nonconforming assignment, buffer mismatch, or an unmatched blocking receive.

The GNU-version test checks __GNUC_MINOR__ >= 8 even for major versions above 4, so many modern GNU compilers retain the fallback backtrace routine that intentionally dereferences a null pointer on every normal halt.
The wrapper unconditionally calls MPI_Init and MPI_Finalize without checking MPI_Initialized or MPI_Finalized, which makes it unsafe to embed in a host that owns the MPI lifecycle.
MPI return codes are repeatedly written to local variables and never checked, so failed collectives or point-to-point operations can silently leave state invalid or ranks divergent.

Automatic processor-grid selection computes border lengths in default integers and uses a hard-coded 1000000000 sentinel, so sufficiently large grid dimensions can overflow or fail to select a factorization.
The integer*8 broadcast relies on the nonstandard MPI_INTEGER8 datatype name and nonstandard kind syntax rather than matching a selected Fortran kind to an MPI datatype.

Character broadcast sends the root's trimmed length but never verifies that receiving character variables are at least that long before assigning x(i:i), so differing declared lengths can write out of bounds.

Every sendrecv overload derives both the send and receive MPI counts solely from size(sendbuf) and never checks recvbuf size, so a mismatched caller can overrun or incompletely fill the receive object.
The basic shift routines index fixed interior rows or columns such as 2, m-1, and n-1 without enforcing minimum extents, so small local partitions can access outside their arrays.

The ranged shift routines accept arbitrary i1/i2 and derive sections using a fixed four-cell overlap without validating ordering or array extents; the rank-3 version is additionally marked in-source as not correct.

xmpi_getrow does not validate prow, n, size(a,2), or size(b), so invalid metadata can yield an invalid source rank, shape-nonconforming assignment, buffer mismatch, or a blocking receive that never matches.
The module unconditionally sets DEBUG level and adds a new stream handler at import time, so reloads or application-level logging configuration can produce duplicate or unexpectedly verbose output.

The explicit unload path assumes a Unix-style libdl and repeatedly calls dlclose based on an external lsof/grep probe, which is not a reliable or portable library-lifetime contract (notably on Windows and systems without lsof).
isloaded interpolates an unquoted absolute library path into a shell command, so spaces or shell metacharacters in a legitimate path can make the load check incorrect.
Construction changes the process-wide current directory, records the prior directory in olddir, but never restores it during finalize.
Name lookup ignores the returned length and any native status while returning name.value, leaving truncation or failed native lookup indistinguishable from a valid name.

Character parameter retrieval allocates only one c_char and passes it as the native output buffer even though valuelength is returned after the call, so a multi-character native result can overwrite the Python-owned object.
ctypes c_char.value is bytes on Python 3, but all type-code branches compare it with text strings, causing valid native type codes to fall through as unsupported.
get_parameters returns a set of (name, value) tuples rather than the mapping implied by the method name and by the neighboring get_arrays implementation.
Integer retrieval rejects ranks above 2 while set_array permits integer ranks through 4, leaving the public get/set array capabilities asymmetric without explanation.

The dynamically selected array functions are declared with POINTER(ndpointer) and invoked through an extra byref layer, an unusual pointer-to-pointer signature whose compatibility with the native routines is unclear and is not validated by status or restype declarations.
Shape compatibility is enforced only with assert, so optimized Python execution removes this guard before native memory is passed.
For a rank-zero integer array, set_array selects c_double instead of c_int, passing scalar storage with the wrong native representation to set0dintarray.
set_array has no unsupported-type else branch, so an unexpected native type code reaches function-name construction with dtype and typename uninitialized.

set_array does not convert or explicitly reject ordinary C-contiguous NumPy arrays before binding them to an F_CONTIGUOUS ndpointer, making accepted ndarray inputs dependent on a late ctypes conversion failure.
